mainTopic: Mixed intentions in bird offerings, and how the bird עולה is offered: מליקה, draining the blood, and removing the crop
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about bird offerings and then begins the גמרא on it. The משנה first explains that a bird חטאת with a שלא לשמה intention mixed in can never become פיגול. It then rules that mixing a wrong-place intention with a wrong-time intention makes the offering פסול without כרת. רבי יהודה says the first intention decides, and the חכמים say order does not matter. Half a כזית for eating and half for burning do not combine, so the offering stays כשר. The גמרא then reads the פסוקים of the bird עולה word by word: one bird is enough, a כהן must do the מליקה with his own body, the head is pinched from the back of the neck and fully separated, and the blood is drained on the upper wall from the סובב. רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב hold that the whole service must be at the top of the מזבח, and אביי and רבא explain the practical difference between the views. Finally, ברייתות explain how the crop is removed together with its feathers.

steps.title: When the permitting act of a bird sin offering was not done properly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three ways a bird חטאת can have a שלא לשמה intention mixed into the מליקה or the מיצוי. In each case the offering's permitting act was not done properly, so it cannot become פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bird sin offering where he pinched the neck not for its sake and squeezed out the blood with intent for beyond its time; or he pinched with intent for beyond its time and squeezed out the blood not for its sake; or he pinched and squeezed out the blood both not for its sake: in all these, the permitting act was not offered properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list. It defines what counts as a bird חטאת whose permitting act was "not offered as it should be."
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת must be brought לשמה, and an intention of שלא לשמה disqualifies it by itself. פיגול only works when everything else about the offering is done properly. Once a שלא לשמה intention is mixed in at either stage, the offering is already ruined in another way, so the intention of beyond its time cannot make it פיגול with כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird sin offering
He pinched the bird's neck with his fingernail (the bird's way of slaughter)
He squeezed the blood out onto the altar
Not for its sake, meaning with the offering's purpose in mind as a different kind of offering
Beyond its time, meaning intending to eat or burn it after the allowed time
The permitting act, the step that makes the offering allowed

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean an intention of beyond its time is harmless here. The offering is still disqualified. It just cannot reach the special status of פיגול that brings כרת.

phrases.english: A bird sin offering that he pinched not for its sake,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, using the feminine form to match חטאת.

phrases.english: and squeezed out the blood with intent for beyond its time;
or where he pinched with intent for beyond its time,
and squeezed out its blood not for its sake;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּלַק וּמִיצָּה הַדָּם שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ –
phrases.english: or where he pinched and squeezed out the blood, both not for its sake:
this is a case where the permitting act was not offered according to its מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier part of the משנה, which made פיגול depend on the permitting act being offered properly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird חטאת with a שלא לשמה intention at the מליקה or the מיצוי has not had its permitting act offered properly, so it cannot become פיגול.

steps.title: Mixing an intention about place with an intention about time
steps.stepSummary: If he intended to eat part of the offering outside its place and part after its time, in either order, the offering is פסול but there is no כרת. This holds whether each part is a full כזית or each is half a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he intended to eat a כזית outside and a כזית tomorrow, or a כזית tomorrow and a כזית outside, or half a כזית outside and half a כזית tomorrow, or half a כזית tomorrow and half a כזית outside, the offering is disqualified, and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new ruling about a mixed intention, where one part is about the wrong place and one part is about the wrong time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An intention about the wrong place only makes the offering פסול. An intention about the wrong time can make it פיגול, but only if no other disqualifying intention is mixed in. Here the place intention spoils the offering, so the time intention cannot bring כרת. Even the two half-כזית intentions combine to make it פסול, because both are disqualifying intentions.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's volume, the minimum amount that counts
Outside, meaning outside the place where it may be eaten
Tomorrow, meaning after the time allowed for eating it
Half an olive's volume
Disqualified
Spiritual excision, the punishment for eating פיגול

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the dispute that follows: does the order of the two intentions matter?

phrases.english: If he intended to eat an olive-bulk outside and an olive-bulk tomorrow,
or an olive-bulk tomorrow and an olive-bulk outside,

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר,
phrases.english: or half an olive-bulk outside and half an olive-bulk tomorrow,

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ –
phrases.english: or half an olive-bulk tomorrow and half an olive-bulk outside:
it is disqualified, and there is no karet for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mixing in a שלא לשמה intention to mixing a place intention with a time intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mixed intention of place and time, in either order and in any amount, makes the offering פסול with no כרת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the first intention decides
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives a rule. If the time intention came first, the offering is פיגול with כרת. If the place intention came first, it is only פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said, this is the rule: if the thought about time came before the thought about place, it is פיגול and one is liable to כרת for it. If the thought about place came before the thought about time, it is disqualified and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the ruling just given and says the order of the intentions matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the first intention a person has determines what happens to the offering. If time came first, פיגול already took hold, and the later place intention cannot undo it. If place came first, the offering was already spoiled, so the later time intention cannot create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
An intention about the wrong time
An intention about the wrong place
Came first, preceded
An offering ruined by a wrong-time intention; eating it brings כרת

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: this is the principle:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַזְּמַן קָדְמָה לְמַחְשֶׁבֶת הַמָּקוֹם –
phrases.english: if the intent about time came before the intent about place,
it is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַמָּקוֹם קָדְמָה לְמַחְשֶׁבֶת הַזְּמַן –
phrases.english: And if the intent about place came before the intent about time,
it is disqualified, and there is no karet for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the anonymous ruling of step 2 by making the outcome depend on order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first intention decides: time first means פיגול with כרת, and place first means only פסול.

steps.title: The חכמים: both orders are only disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold that whether time or place came first, the offering is פסול with no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: in both this case and that case, it is disqualified and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים respond to רבי יהודה and reject his distinction about order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same position as the anonymous ruling in step 2. For the חכמים, as long as a place intention is mixed in anywhere, the time intention cannot make the offering פיגול. Order makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
This and that, meaning both cases

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. רבי יהודה says the first intention decides. The חכמים (and the first ruling of the משנה) say any mix of place and time means פסול with no כרת.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
phrases.notes: This line is in square brackets: it's in the corrected wording but not in every printing.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה וָזֶה פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת.]
phrases.english: in both this case and that, it is disqualified and there is no karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: זֶה וָזֶה פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה and goes back to the ruling of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order does not matter: any mix of a place intention and a time intention is פסול with no כרת.

steps.title: Eating and burning do not add up
steps.stepSummary: If he intended to eat half a כזית and burn half a כזית improperly, the offering stays כשר, because eating and burning do not combine to make a full כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he intended to eat half a כזית and to burn half a כזית improperly, the offering is valid, because eating and burning do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a final ruling, a case where the improper intentions do not even disqualify the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An improper intention only counts if it covers at least a כזית. Two halves of the same kind of act can combine, as we saw in step 2. Eating and burning are different acts, though, so the halves do not combine, nothing reaches a כזית, and the offering stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: To burn on the altar
Eating and burning
Join together, combine into one amount
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 2, where two halves did combine. There both halves were about eating. Here one is eating and one is burning, and those do not combine.
steps.whatToRemember: An improper intention needs a full כזית, and only intentions about the same kind of act (eating with eating) can be added together to reach it.

phrases.aramaic: לֶאֱכוֹל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וּלְהַקְטִיר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת –
phrases.english: If he intended to eat half an olive-bulk and to burn half an olive-bulk,
it is valid, because eating and burning do not join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the half-כזית cases of step 2 and limits when halves can combine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half a כזית for eating and half a כזית for burning do not combine, so the offering is כשר.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'and he shall bring it'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא asking what the word 'והקריבו' in the bird עולה פסוק comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Sages taught: "And he shall bring it." What does this word come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion with a ברייתא that asks why one word in the פסוק is needed. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous פסוק already said the person brings his offering, so 'והקריבו' looks extra. When a word looks extra, the ברייתא expects it to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
And he shall bring it
What does the verse come to teach?

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
"And he shall bring it": what does the verse come to teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה about bird offerings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the seemingly extra word 'והקריבו' teaches.

steps.title: Even a single bird may be donated
steps.stepSummary: The previous פסוק uses plural words for the birds, so one might think a donor must bring at least two. 'והקריבו' is singular and teaches that even one bird is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says "Then he shall bring of the turtledoves or of the young pigeons," one might think that a person donating a bird may not bring fewer than two. So the verse says "and he shall bring it," which teaches that he may bring even one single bird to the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question: the word 'והקריבו' teaches that one bird alone is a valid donation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוק uses plural words, 'turtledoves' and 'young pigeons,' which could suggest a minimum of two birds. 'והקריבו' means 'bring IT,' in the singular, and that removes the mistaken idea.

keyTerms.meaning: One who donates a voluntary offering
A single bird, not one of a pair
Turtledoves
Young pigeons

phrases.english: Since it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהִקְרִיב מִן הַתֹּרִים אוֹ מִן בְּנֵי הַיּוֹנָה״
phrases.english: "Then he shall bring of the turtledoves or of the young pigeons"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:14. Both bird words here are plural.

phrases.english: one might think that a person who donates a bird
may not bring fewer than two birds?
So the verse says: "And he shall bring it"

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ פְּרִידָה אַחַת יָבִיא אֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: meaning he may bring even one single bird to the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'והקריבו' teaches that one may donate even a single bird.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'the priest'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק mentions 'הכהן' and answers that it teaches a כהן is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the verse say "the priest"? To require a priest for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next word in the פסוק and says that 'הכהן' teaches that only a כהן may do the מליקה. It then sets up the reason this word is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is new: the bird's main act must be done by a כהן. The next step explains why we could not have known this without the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The priest
To set as a fixed requirement

phrases.english: Why does the verse say "the priest"?
To require a priest for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next word in the same פסוק.

steps.title: A קל וחומר says a bird should not need a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows why the פסוק is needed. A קל וחומר from a sheep offering would have taught that a bird does not need a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might have thought: isn't it logical? If a sheep offering, for which the Torah required the north, did not require a priest, then a bird, for which the Torah did not require the north, should surely not require a priest!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא builds a logical argument, a קל וחומר, that points the opposite way, to show why the פסוק had to say 'הכהן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sheep עולה is the stricter case because it must be slaughtered in the צפון, yet its שחיטה may be done by a non-כהן. A bird has no צפון rule, so it looks more lenient, and logic would say it surely needs no כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? (opens a קל וחומר)
A sheep or goat offering
The north side of the עזרה, where certain offerings are slaughtered

steps.confusionAlert: This קל וחומר is NOT the final halacha. The ברייתא brings it only to show that without the פסוק we would have made this mistake.

phrases.english: For one might have thought: isn't it logical?

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בֶּן צֹאן, שֶׁקָּבַע לוֹ צָפוֹן
phrases.english: If a sheep offering, for which the Torah required the north,
did not require a priest;
then a bird, for which the Torah did not require the north,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יִקְבַּע לוֹ כֹּהֵן?!
phrases.english: isn't it logical that it should not require a priest?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the teaching of step 8 needed a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a bird needs a כהן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sheep is stricter (it needs צפון) yet does not need a כהן. A bird is more lenient, so it should not need a כהן either.

steps.title: The פסוק overrides the logic: a כהן is required
steps.stepSummary: The word 'הכהן' in the פסוק teaches that a כהן is required, against the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the verse says "the priest," to require a priest for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the logical argument by pointing to the פסוק, which clearly requires a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where a פסוק says something directly, a קל וחומר cannot stand against it. That is why the Torah had to write 'הכהן'.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse comes to teach

steps.whatToRemember: A bird offering may be a single bird, and its מליקה must be done by a כהן, even though a sheep's שחיטה may be done by a non-כהן.

phrases.english: So the verse says: "the priest"
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets appears in some printings, but the corrected text leaves it out.

phrases.english: to require a priest for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the logical argument.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bird would not need a כהן because of the קל וחומר from a sheep.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'הכהן' requires a כהן for the bird.

steps.title: A קל וחומר suggests מליקה needs a knife
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that מליקה should need a tool like a knife, based on a קל וחומר from שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he can pinch it with a knife. And it is logical: if slaughtering, for which the Torah did not require a priest, did require an instrument, then pinching, which the Torah did require a priest for, should surely require an instrument!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new possibility: maybe מליקה must be done with a knife. It backs this up with a קל וחומר, and steps 12–14 answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic flips the earlier one. שחיטה is the more lenient act because a non-כהן may do it, yet it needs a כלי. מליקה is stricter because it needs a כהן, so it should surely need a כלי too.

keyTerms.meaning: Killing a bird offering by pinching the nape with the כהן's fingernail
Knife
Ritual slaughter
An instrument or tool

phrases.english: One might think he can pinch it with a knife?
And it is logical:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אִם שְׁחִיטָה, שֶׁלֹּא קָבַע לָהּ כֹּהֵן
phrases.english: If slaughtering, for which the Torah did not require a priest,
did require an instrument;
then pinching, which the Torah did require a priest for,
isn't it logical that it should require an instrument?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 10 (מליקה needs a כהן) to build a new קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: How מליקה is done, by hand or with a knife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שחיטה is more lenient (no כהן needed) yet needs a כלי, so the stricter מליקה should need a כלי too.

steps.title: The verse says 'כהן... ומלק'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers the קל וחומר that מליקה should need a tool by quoting 'כהן... ומלק'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'The כהן... shall pinch off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea from step 11 that מליקה needs a knife by pointing to the פסוק. Exactly how the פסוק teaches this comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 argued that if שחיטה needs a tool, מליקה surely does too. The ברייתא answers with the words 'כהן' and 'ומלק' placed side by side. רבי עקיבא will explain why these words show that no tool is used.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching the back of a bird's neck. This is how a bird קרבן is killed.
'And he shall pinch off'. The verb in the פסוק.

phrases.english: The verse states: "The Kohen... and pinch off."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר from שחיטה raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides a קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מליקה needs a tool, like שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that מליקה is done without a tool.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks why the verse needs to say 'כהן'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא points out that everyone already knows a זר cannot serve at the מזבח, so the word 'כהן' must teach something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: Could you really think that a זר may come near the מזבח? So why does the verse say 'כהן'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא asks why the פסוק says 'כהן' when it is obvious that only a כהן serves at the מזבח. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody would think a זר may offer קרבנות. So the word 'כהן' cannot just be telling us who does the job. It must be telling us how the job is done.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is not a כהן.
The altar.
'Could it enter your mind?' Used to show that an idea is obviously wrong.

steps.confusionAlert: Step 10 used the word 'הכהן' to teach that a כהן is required. רבי עקיבא says nobody needs a פסוק for that, since a זר may not serve at the מזבח anyway. So he reads 'כהן' next to 'ומלק' (ויקרא 1:15) as teaching how the מליקה is done.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
Could it enter your mind
that a non-Kohen may approach the altar?!
Rather, why does the verse state "Kohen"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 12 teaches its lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra lesson does the word 'כהן' teach, since it is obvious that only a כהן serves?

steps.title: The pinching is done with the כהן's own body
steps.stepSummary: The word 'כהן' teaches that the מליקה must be done by the כהן himself, not with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that the pinching must be done with the כהן's own body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers that 'כהן' next to 'ומלק' means the כהן pinches with his own self. This finishes the answer to step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word cannot be teaching who does the job, it teaches how: with the כהן's own body. That rules out a knife and overrides the קל וחומר from שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: With the כהן's own body, not with a tool.

steps.whatToRemember: מליקה is done by the כהן with his own body. Unlike שחיטה, no tool is used.

phrases.english: That the pinching must be with the very body of the Kohen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's question from step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'כהן' teaches that the מליקה is done with the כהן's own body, without a tool.

steps.title: Maybe the pinching can be done high or low on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that perhaps the מליקה may be done anywhere on the מזבח, higher or lower.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he may pinch it either above or below.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new possible mistake about where on the מזבח the מליקה is done. The next step uses the פסוק to correct it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic: place, not method. Without a source, one might think any spot on the מזבח is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think'. Introduces a wrong idea that the ברייתא will reject.
Above... below.

phrases.english: One might think he may pinch it
whether above or below?
phrases.notes: This means higher or lower on the wall of the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the מליקה is done to where it is done.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With no limit stated, maybe any height on the מזבח works.

steps.title: Pinching is on top of the altar, like the burning
steps.stepSummary: Because 'ומלק' is next to 'והקטיר', the מליקה must be at the top of the מזבח, where the burning happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And pinch off... and burn it.' Just as burning is on top of the altar, so too pinching is on top of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by linking two words that sit next to each other in the פסוק. מליקה goes where הקטרה goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places מליקה and הקטרה side by side, so they share a rule. הקטרה is clearly on top of the מזבח, so מליקה is too.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the קרבן on the מזבח.
The top of the altar.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And pinch off... and burn it" –
just as burning is on top of the altar,
so too pinching is on top of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning from words placed side by side in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מליקה may be done at any height on the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: מליקה must be on top of the מזבח, like הקטרה.

steps.title: Pinching is from the back of the neck
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that 'ומלק' means pinching from the back of the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And pinch off' means from the back of the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states a new rule: the מליקה is done from the back of the neck. The next steps look for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is now the third detail about מליקה: where on the bird it is done. The ברייתא states the rule first and then proves it.

keyTerms.meaning: Facing the back of the neck (the nape).

phrases.english: "And pinch off" – at the nape of the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new detail about where on the bird the מליקה is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מליקה of an עולת העוף is done from the back of the neck.

steps.title: Maybe it is from the front of the neck
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know it is the back of the neck and not the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say from the back of the neck. Or perhaps it is only from the throat?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own rule from step 17 and asks for a source. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ומלק' in the עולה פסוק does not say which side of the neck. So the throat side seems possible too.

keyTerms.meaning: The throat, the front of the neck.
'You say... or perhaps it is only...'. A formula that asks for proof.

phrases.english: You say at the nape;
or perhaps it is only from the throat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר מִמּוּל עוֹרֶף; אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִן הַצַּוָּאר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What proves the מליקה is at the back of the neck and not the throat?

steps.title: Learning from the bird חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The same word 'ומלק' appears by חטאת העוף, where the פסוק says 'ממול ערפו'. So the עולה is also pinched from the back of the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical: 'and pinch off' is said here, and 'and pinch off' is said there. Just as there it is at the nape, so too here it is at the nape.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the rule by matching the same word in two places. The פסוק about חטאת העוף clearly says the back of the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By חטאת העוף (ויקרא 5:8) the פסוק says 'ומלק את ראשו ממול ערפו'. Since the עולה פסוק uses the same word 'ומלק', it shares that detail.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is logical'. Introduces a reasoned proof.
'Here... there'. Compares two places in the תורה.
A bird brought as a חטאת.

phrases.english: And it is logical:
it is stated here "and pinch off,"
and it is stated there "and pinch off";
just as there it is at the nape,
so too here it is at the nape!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared word 'ומלק' links the עולה to the חטאת, which is pinched from the back of the neck.

steps.title: Then maybe the head is not separated either
steps.stepSummary: If we learn from חטאת העוף, perhaps the עולה head should also stay attached, as it does by the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there he pinches but does not separate, so too here he should pinch and not separate?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the comparison from step 19. If we copy one detail from the חטאת, maybe we must copy its other detail too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By חטאת העוף the פסוק says 'ולא יבדיל': the head stays attached. A full comparison would bring that rule over to the עולה as well. The next step must block this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so'. Pushes an argument to its next result.
Separates (the head from the body).

phrases.aramaic: אִי – מָה לְהַלָּן מוֹלֵק וְאֵינוֹ מַבְדִּיל,
phrases.english: If so – just as there he pinches but does not separate,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:8 says 'ולא יבדיל': the חטאת head stays attached.

phrases.english: so too here he should pinch and not separate?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי – מָה לְהַלָּן מוֹלֵק וְאֵינוֹ מַבְדִּיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between עולת העוף and חטאת העוף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חטאת rule about the back of the neck carries over, its rule against separating should carry over too.

steps.title: The head is fully separated, like the burning
steps.stepSummary: Since 'ומלק' is next to 'והקטיר', and the head and body are burned separately, the head must be fully separated at the מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And pinch off and burn it.' Just as in burning the head is by itself and the body by itself, so too in pinching the head is by itself and the body by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא blocks the challenge by again linking מליקה to הקטרה. In an עולה, the head comes off completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the עולת העוף, the head and body are burned separately. Because מליקה is placed next to הקטרה, the head must already be separated at the מליקה. So the עולה shares only the back-of-the-neck rule with the חטאת, not the 'do not separate' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The head by itself and the body by itself. They are fully separated.

steps.whatToRemember: עולת העוף: the כהן pinches with his own body, on top of the מזבח, from the back of the neck, and fully separates the head. חטאת העוף shares the back-of-the-neck rule, but its head is not separated.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two birds. Both are pinched from the back of the neck, but only by the עולה is the head taken off completely.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And pinch off and burn it";

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקְטָרָה – הָרֹאשׁ לְעַצְמוֹ וְהַגּוּף לְעַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: just as with burning – the head is by itself and the body by itself,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מְלִיקָה – הָרֹאשׁ לְעַצְמוֹ וְהַגּוּף לְעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: so too with pinching – the head is by itself and the body by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning from words placed side by side in the פסוק limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עולה head stays attached, like the חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עולה head is fully separated, just as the head and body are burned separately.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the head and body are burned separately?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that the head of the bird is burned by itself and the body is burned by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that the head is burned by itself and the body is burned by itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question to back up what it said in the last step: that the head and body are burned separately. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 relied on the idea that the head and body are burned separately. Now the ברייתא stops to ask: where in the פסוק do we actually see that?

keyTerms.meaning: Burning (an offering on the מזבח)
The head (of the bird)
The body (of the bird)
By itself

phrases.english: And from where do we know that the burning of the head is by itself
and the body is burned by itself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption the ברייתא used in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows the head and the body are burned separately.

steps.title: Two mentions of burning, one for the body and one for the head
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'והקטיר אותו' already covers burning the body, so the earlier 'והקטיר המזבחה' must be about burning the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says, 'and he shall burn it.' That covers the burning of the body. So how do I explain the earlier words, 'and he shall burn it on the מזבח'? That פסוק must be talking about burning the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: the תורה mentions burning twice, so one mention must be for the body and the other for the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is one mention of burning in the later פסוק, which is about the body, and another in the earlier פסוק, right after the מליקה. Since the body already has its own mention, the earlier one must be teaching a separate burning of the head. Two separate burnings means the head and the body are burned separately.

keyTerms.meaning: It is already stated (covered)
How do I explain (this extra phrase)?
The פסוק is talking about

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'And he shall burn it'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:17, after the bird's wings are torn. This is about the body.

phrases.english: so the burning of the body is already stated;
so how do I explain
'and he shall burn it on the altar'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:15, right after the head is pinched off.

phrases.english: The verse is speaking about the burning of the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The burning in ויקרא 1:15 is the head, and the burning in 1:17 is the body. They are two separate burnings.

steps.title: All the blood, and only on the wall of the altar
steps.stepSummary: 'ונמצה דמו' means all the blood must be drained, and 'על קיר המזבח' excludes the wall of the ramp and the wall of the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And its blood shall be drained out' means all of it. 'On the wall of the altar' means not on the wall of the ramp and not on the wall of the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to the next words of the פסוק and explains two details about draining the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דמו' (its blood) is read as 'all its blood', so the כהן must drain it fully. The words 'קיר המזבח' (wall of the altar) rule out other walls nearby, such as the ramp or the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: And it shall be drained/squeezed out
Wall
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
The Sanctuary building

phrases.english: 'And its blood shall be drained out' – all of it.
'On the wall of the altar'
– and not on the wall of the ramp,
and not on the wall of the Sanctuary;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the פסוק after finishing the topic of burning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the blood must be drained, and only onto the wall of the מזבח.

steps.title: Which wall of the altar? The upper wall
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that the wall meant here is the upper wall of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which wall is this? This is the upper wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks which part of the מזבח wall the פסוק means and answers: the upper part. The next steps will challenge and then prove this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wall of the מזבח has an upper part and a lower part, divided by a red line (חוט הסיקרא). The ברייתא rules that the blood of the עולת העוף goes on the upper part.

keyTerms.meaning: And which one is this?
The upper wall (above the red line)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with an animal עולה, whose blood goes on the LOWER part. The bird עולה is different, and the next steps deal with exactly this point.

phrases.english: And which is this?
This is the upper wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down which part of the wall from Step 24 is meant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood of the עולת העוף is drained on the upper wall of the מזבח.

steps.title: Logic suggests the lower wall instead
steps.stepSummary: A logical argument suggests the lower wall: for animals, the חטאת is above and the עולה is below. For birds, the חטאת is already below, so surely the עולה should be below too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it means only the lower wall? And it makes sense: for an animal, whose חטאת is above, its עולה is below. So for a bird, whose חטאת is below, isn't it logical that its עולה is below too?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own ruling with a logical argument for the lower wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument says the עולה is always 'lower' than or equal to the חטאת. For animals, the חטאת goes up and the עולה goes down. For birds, the חטאת already goes down, so the bird עולה should certainly go down as well. This attacks the ruling of Step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower wall (below the red line)
And it is logical (an argument from reasoning)
An animal offering
A bird offering

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only the lower wall?
And it is logical:
If an animal, whose sin offering is above,
– its burnt offering is below;
a bird, whose sin offering is below,
– is it not logical that its burnt offering is below?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 25 with a logical argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the blood of the bird עולה goes on the upper wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Comparing to animal offerings, an עולה is never higher than its matching חטאת. Since the bird חטאת is below, the bird עולה should be below too.

steps.title: The order of the verse puts the draining at the top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists burning before draining. That can't be the real order, so it teaches that the draining happens at the top of the מזבח, just like the burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he shall pinch, and burn, and its blood shall be drained.' Could you really think that after burning he goes back and drains the blood? Rather, it is telling you: just as the burning is on top of the מזבח, so too the draining is on top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the logical argument with a proof from the פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the blood obviously can't be drained after the bird is burned, the order of the words must be teaching something else. Putting the draining next to the burning links them: both happen at the top of the מזבח. A clear פסוק beats the logical argument, so the upper wall stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (to counter that argument)
Could it enter your mind?
Draining/squeezing out the blood
The top of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The bird עולה's blood goes on the upper wall. We learn it from the פסוק putting 'והקטיר' right before 'ונמצה': both happen up high.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'And pinch... and burn... and its blood shall be drained'
– could it enter your mind
that after he burned it, he goes back and drains it?!
Rather, it is to tell you:
just as the burning is on top of the altar,
so too the draining is on top of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 26 with a proof from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic would place the bird עולה's blood on the lower wall, like the bird חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק links draining to burning, so the draining is at the top of the מזבח, on the upper wall.

steps.title: How the כהן actually did it
steps.stepSummary: The כהן went up the ramp, turned onto the ledge to the southeast corner, pinched off the head from the back of the neck, separated it, and drained the blood on the wall of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How was it done? He would go up the ramp, turn onto the ledge, and come to the southeast corner. He would pinch off its head from the back of its neck and separate it, and drain its blood on the wall of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now describes, step by step, the practical way the כהן offered the bird עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing on the סובב (the ledge around the מזבח), the wall next to him is the upper part, so the blood lands up high. This also puts into practice the earlier rules: pinching from the back of the neck and fully separating the head.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introducing the practical procedure)
The ledge running around the מזבח
The southeast corner
From the back of its neck
Separates (the head from the body)

phrases.english: How so?
He would go up the ramp
and turn to the ledge,
and come to the southeast corner;

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מוֹלֵק אֶת רֹאשָׁהּ מִמּוּל עׇרְפָּה
phrases.english: he would pinch off its head from the back of its neck
and separate it,
and drain its blood on the wall of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows in practice how the draining on top of the מזבח (Step 27) is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן offers the bird עולה from the ledge at the southeast corner, separating the head and draining the blood on the upper wall.

steps.title: Even if done a bit lower, it is still valid
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן drained the blood below his feet, even a full אמה lower, the offering is still כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did it below his feet, even an אמה lower, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a ruling for after the fact: draining the blood somewhat lower than ideal does not ruin the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ideal is to drain the blood right next to where the כהן stands on the ledge. But if the blood went lower, even an אמה below his feet, the offering is still כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Below his feet
A cubit (a measure of about an arm's length)
Valid (the offering is acceptable)

steps.whatToRemember: Ideally the blood is drained right at the level of the ledge, on the upper wall. But even an אמה lower is still כשר after the fact.

phrases.english: If he did it below his feet,
even a cubit lower – it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an after-the-fact leniency to the procedure in Step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Draining the blood below the כהן's feet, even by an אמה, is still כשר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ideal place is beside the ledge, but a little lower does not ruin the offering.

steps.title: The whole bird offering is done only at the top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב say that every part of the bird עולה is done only at the top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב say: the entire bird burnt-offering is done only at the top of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by quoting two תנאים who disagree with the lenient ruling from Step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 said that draining the blood even an אמה below the כהן's feet is still כשר. These תנאים are stricter. Every part of the bird עולה must happen at the top of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The top of the altar

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov say:
Its entire [service] is not performed
phrases.notes: "Its" means the bird עולה. Literally, "all of itself."

phrases.english: except at the top of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion to the leniency in Step 29
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole bird עולה must be done at the top of the מזבח.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the first תנא and רבי נחמיה with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step. Both sides seem to agree that the bird is done at the top, so what are they arguing about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא also said the draining is done on the upper wall (Steps 25–27), and the burning is at the top. So the גמרא wants to find the actual case where the two views give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is [the difference] between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between Step 29 and Step 30
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what practical case do the first תנא and the dissenting תנאים disagree?

steps.title: The difference is setting up a wood-pile on the ledge
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא say the two views disagree about whether the כהן may set up a fire on the סובב and burn the bird there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: the difference between them is whether one may make a wood-pile on top of the ledge.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא answer the question from Step 31. The argument is about building a fire on the סובב, the ledge that runs around the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא allows a wood-pile on the סובב when needed. That is why blood drained below where the כהן stands is still כשר. רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב never allow burning on the סובב, so for them everything must be at the very top.

keyTerms.meaning: An arranged pile of wood for the fire
The ledge running around the middle of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The two views agree that the bird belongs on top. They disagree about whether a fire may ever be set up on the סובב.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:
making a wood-pile on top of the ledge
is [the difference] between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 31
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether a wood-pile may be set up on the סובב for burning the bird.

steps.title: The crop is removed: the verse about the body of the bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about the bird's body. It quotes a ברייתא explaining that מֻרְאָתוֹ in the פסוק means the crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He came to the body, etc." The Rabbis taught: "And he shall remove its מֻרְאָתוֹ with its feathers": this means the crop.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. The גמרא quotes the משנה about the body of the bird and brings a ברייתא that explains a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rare word מֻרְאָתוֹ is identified as the זפק, the crop: the pouch in the bird's throat where food is stored. This sets up the next question about how the crop is removed.

keyTerms.meaning: The body of the bird
A word in the פסוק that refers to the crop
The crop, a food pouch in a bird's throat

phrases.english: "He came to the body, etc."
The Rabbis taught:
"And he shall remove its murato with its feathers"
this is the crop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מֻרְאָתוֹ in the פסוק refers to the crop.

steps.title: Might he just cut out the crop with a knife?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possible first thought: maybe the כהן may simply cut around the crop with a knife and remove it alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he may cut around it with a knife and take it out?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests a possible way of removing the crop so that the next step can reject it with the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only said "its crop," we could think removing just the crop is enough, done neatly with a knife. This is the הוה אמינא, the first thought that the פסוק is about to correct.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (a first thought about to be rejected)
Cut around in a circle
Knife

phrases.english: One might think he cuts around [it] with a knife and takes it?
phrases.notes: יקדיר means cutting in a circle around the crop, taking out only the crop itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible way of removing the crop
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is cutting out the crop alone with a knife enough?

steps.title: The crop is removed together with its feathers
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "with its feathers," which teaches that the כהן takes the feathered skin along with the crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "with its feathers": he takes the feathers along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the first thought from Step 34 using the word בנוצתה in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word בנוצתה shows that cutting out only the crop is not enough. The כהן must remove the crop with the skin and feathers still attached.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces the proof)
Feathers

steps.whatToRemember: The crop is removed together with its feathers and skin, not cut out alone with a knife.

phrases.english: The verse says: "with its feathers"
he takes the feathers along with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first thought of Step 34 using the פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No; the crop must be taken out together with the feathers.

steps.title: The gizzard is removed too
steps.stepSummary: אבא יוסי בן חנן says the כהן removes the crop and the gizzard along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא יוסי בן חנן says: he takes the crop and takes its gizzard with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion is quoted about what exactly gets removed from the bird's body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view spoke about the crop with its feathers. אבא יוסי בן חנן adds another part: the gizzard (the bird's muscular stomach) is also removed together with the crop.

keyTerms.meaning: Gizzard, the bird's muscular stomach

phrases.english: Abba Yosei ben Chanan says:
He takes it and takes its gizzard with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another opinion that adds the gizzard
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gizzard is removed together with the crop.

steps.title: Cutting a Window Around the Crop
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads בְּנֹצָתָהּ as 'its feathers.' It teaches that the כהן cuts a window-shaped opening with a knife to take out the crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'בְּנֹצָתָהּ' means 'with its feathers.' The כהן cuts it with a knife in the shape of a window.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more teaching about how to remove the bird's crop. This one comes from the school of רבי ישמעאל, and it explains the word בְּנֹצָתָהּ in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בְּנֹצָתָהּ is read as two words joined together: בְּנוֹצָה שֶׁלָּהּ, 'with its feathers.' From this, the כהן does not pull out the crop by itself. He cuts a window-shaped opening through the skin and feathers right over the crop, and takes them out together with it. This is a different picture from אבא יוסי בן חנן, who said the gizzard also comes out.

keyTerms.meaning: The study house (school) of רבי ישמעאל
With its feathers (from the פסוק)
He cuts around it / carves it out
Knife
A window or opening

steps.whatToRemember: According to the school of רבי ישמעאל, the כהן cuts a window-shaped hole and removes the crop together with the skin and feathers right over it.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Benotzatah" means "with its feathers";
phrases.notes: They read the one word in the פסוק (ויקרא 1:16) as two words squeezed together: 'with feathers' + 'its.'

phrases.english: he cuts it with a knife in the shape of a window.
phrases.notes: He means a window-shaped hole right over the crop, so only the skin and feathers there come out with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אבא יוסי בן חנן's view in step 36, this gives another ברייתא's way of reading בְּנֹצָתָהּ and of how the crop is removed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בְּנֹצָתָהּ means 'its feathers.' The כהן cuts a window-shaped opening with a knife and removes the crop together with the feathered skin over it.
